payload.name: SearchActivityFactsAcrossPredicates
payload.description: When answering what activities/hobbies a person pursues (with or without an excluded topic), supplement structured predicate='activity' searches with semantic/free-text searches for concrete activity terms across memory kinds.
content: When a question asks what activities or hobbies a person pursues (including 'besides', 'apart from', or 'other than' an excluded topic), do not rely only on structured queries with predicate='activity'; activity facts are often embedded in event/preference/state memories with other predicates or in free-text descriptions.

Run at least one hybrid or semantic/free-text search combining the person's name with concrete activity vocabulary (e.g., running, biking, art, gardening, surfing) and without requiring the words 'activity' or 'hobby' to appear.

Before answering, if the retrieved set is missing concrete activities, widen memory_kinds beyond 'event' to include 'preference', 'profile', and 'state', and re-search each concrete activity name that appears anywhere in the session or evidence.

solves: When generic 'activities' searches miss concrete activities because facts are stored under non-activity predicates (e.g., 'discovered surfing', 'ran a gardening class'), the answer becomes incomplete. This rule supplements structured predicate='activity' queries with semantic/free-text searches for concrete activity terms and checks all memory kinds. Applies to future activity/hobby questions, including 'besides X' variants.
